prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks, from the magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms to fractional uncertainties near 1e-18

statement.case_for: I have moved from B024 to B015 (Katori and Ye) as a single-part prize. The scientific case is the one the five B015 supporters share and I find it sound on the evidence supplied: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice removes the trap light shift while keeping many atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime, and Ye's group realised it at roughly 1e-18 with many-body-limited operation and millimetre-scale gravitational redshift. Independent reproduction at RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and NPL means the result is settled rather than awaiting confirmation. The credit fits two supplied names without forcing anyone out under the three-person limit, which is not true of B024 once Girvin, Huang and the transmon are counted. For the citation I would name the lattice architecture and the 1e-18 realisation explicitly, so that it is visibly distinct from the 2005 comb and the 2012 ion-control prizes.
statement.case_against: Three reservations remain. First, the lattice clock is a measurement capability rather than a new phenomenon, and Danielsson's criterion of prediction followed by surprise is not met in the same way as in B006. Second, the inventor/refiner line is contestable: the Paris and PTB lattice work, Ludlow and Lemke, and the single-ion clock community reached comparable uncertainties by other routes. Third, the SI redefinition of the second is still pending. I weigh these as framing and timing issues, not defects of the science. Separately, my own B024 case has not become weaker on the science. It is still a mature, original step, but its overlap with the 2025 prize and its credit gap are real, and my field proximity makes me a poor judge of how much weight to give it.

responses.point: Kroll asks whether the SI redefinition of the second is a precondition for B015 and whether crediting only Katori and Ye is defensible against Paris, PTB and NIST contributions.
responses.response: On the redefinition I would treat it as supporting, not a precondition. The performance is already independently reproduced and compared internationally, so waiting would add no scientific evidence, and I made the same argument against waiting on B024 in round 1, so I should apply it consistently. On credit, I think a principled line exists on the supplied evidence: Katori for the concept (magic-wavelength trapping) and Ye for taking it to the 1e-18 regime with the many-body physics. The Paris and PTB groups and the ion community demonstrated comparable performance by other routes, which makes them refiners or parallel competitors, not originators of the lattice concept. I withdraw my round-1 point that Kroll's caveat about earlier prizes cuts against B015 in equal measure, because the citation can state what is new.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that the comb made optical frequencies countable and the lattice clock is what is now counted, so a reader would see a distinct step, while warning that a narrow citation might favour neutral atoms over the ion lineage.
responses.response: I accept that framing and it is the main reason I now hold the novelty objection to B015 as answerable. I also take her ion-clock warning seriously, and the way to meet it is a citation that names the lattice architecture explicitly and does not claim to honour optical clocks in general. That leaves the ion route outside the prize without denying it. She also gave the transmon and readout qualification on B024, and her own placement of B024 second with the same 2025 reservation is consistent with my moving it to an alternative.

responses.point: Danielsson prefers B006 as a prediction followed by an unexpected experimental result, and values it above enabling measurement advances.
responses.response: I share his regard for B006 and I rank it as a serious candidate, but I still hold it on maturity: pairing mechanism, correlated-state interpretation and sample disorder are open, and the credit beyond the three names is unresolved. I do not think the distinction between discovery of a phenomenon and invention of an instrument is decisive for B015. The lattice clock produced new physical access, including gravitational redshift across a millimetre sample and many-body effects in the clock, and it is an invention of the kind the prize recognises. If he has evidence that the pairing question is closer to settled than I think, that would shift me on B006 for a later year.

responses.point: Pearce asks the committee to be able to state what is new relative to 2005 and 2012, naming the neutral-atom many-body lattice and the 1e-18 regime rather than clocks in general.
responses.response: I agree and I would adopt that wording in the final citation. His request to disclose field-adjacent interests before B007 and B037 are weighed is also right, and I make my own parallel disclosure for B024 below. On the chair's question about my recusal, I think the cleanest course is that I step back from deliberation on B024 and do not argue for it now that B015 is my preferred configuration.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that a citation naming the lattice architecture and the 1e-18 realisation is distinct enough from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes.
Whether the Paris, PTB, NIST and single-ion contributions weaken the two-name credit more than I judge, since I cannot verify priority details beyond the supplied names.
Whether my move away from B024 reflects the scientific case or my own recusal concern, which I cannot fully separate.
Whether twisted bilayer graphene (B006) becomes clearly mature once the pairing question is better resolved.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure. For B024 I work in circuit and waveguide QED, direct WACQT, and collaborate frequently with Chalmers colleagues in superconducting circuits, including Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson. Chalmers also hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize. My profile records no documented relationship with Blais, Wallraff or Schoelkopf. I propose to recuse from deliberation and voting on B024. For B015 and B010 my profile records no relationship with Katori, Ye, Bloch, Cirac, Zoller or Blatt, though WACQT's quantum-information work is close to B010, and Eva Olsson at Chalmers is a colleague whose preferred configuration is also B015, which I note without any effect on my view.
